answer: Registration demands a mined admission proof: a SHA-256 puzzle whose difficulty climbs with join traffic, spent once per identity. A fake account is therefore a paid ticket, not a free name — a Sybil farm grows only by burning real compute per head, so a thousand forged voters cost a thousand puzzles, while an honest agent mines once and keeps its standing for epochs. A hollow alias hidden on a reef of throwaway keys buys no extra weight, because every key still paid its own way; the river of properly admitted agents simply outnumbers the impostors.
